title: Compost Maturity Hold-Time
dataSources: Hive metrics (`flowhive:reading`), egg counter events (`eggcounter:event`), goat RFID visits (`goattag:scan`), goat watering and feed logs (`goatcare:event`), and compost readings (`compost:reading`).
app: Smallholding and backyard telemetry from Flow Hive scales, chicken coop counters, RFID goat tags, compost thermometers, and camera-driven chore logs sent to Splunk HEC via MQTT and scripted inputs.
spl:
index=personal sourcetype=compost:reading
| search stage="curing" days_in_cure=*
| stats avg(days_in_cure) as avg_days_in_cure perc90(days_in_cure) as p90_days_in_cure count as samples by pile_id
| sort 0 - avg_days_in_cure
description: Measures compost maturity hold time by pile.
value: Hold time in curing helps you avoid using compost that looks done but has not stabilized long enough.
implementation: Send the relevant duration field for compost maturity hold time to `index=personal` and review both average and p90 latency instead of relying on single examples.
visualization: Table of average and p90 compost maturity hold time.
grandmaExplanation: It turns how long compost maturity hold time usually takes, so slowdowns are obvious instead of anecdotal.
